Subject: Finova: Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing - follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on SLO targets and routing logic: 

Call highlights
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) in US/EU; p95 <= 220ms in APAC (the team said they can tolerate slightly higher).
- Peak throughput: ~1,500 reqs/sec across global fleet during market open; steady-state ~300 rps.
- Concurrency: typical per-user concurrency is low (1-3), but bursts to 50-75 concurrent for specific jobs.
- Streaming: required for chat UX - token-level streaming and mid-stream cancellations supported.
- Data residency: EU data must remain in EU region; APAC workloads should process in APAC where possible.

Proposed next steps
1) I attached a short SLO proposal (redwood-slo-proposal.pdf) with recommended instance profiles and routing policy options.
2) Nikhil (cc'd) will follow up with a brief note on required network topology / egress controls for EU-only routing.
3) If the SLOs look good, we can schedule a technical deep-dive next week to validate test harness and run a small perf spike test.
4) Priya / procurement: we'll include the SLA draft (sla-draft.docx) in the next contract packet if you want to start redlines.

Questions for you before the tech deep-dive:
- Can you confirm the expected 99th percentile payload size (average tokens/request)?
- Any hard constraints on cross-region failover (e.g., must never failover out of EU for EU-tagged requests)?

I'll hold a 30-minute slot on Tue/Wed for a deep-dive - send preferred times and we'll lock it in.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Thanks Marissa - this is great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- 99th percentile payload: typically 600-900 tokens during peak (many requests include a small context + customer data). Average closer to 320 tokens.
- For EU data: must remain in EU for both inference and short-term KV cache. We can tolerate async disaster recovery cross-region, but not synchronous failover.
- Streaming: must support chunked token streaming with cancellations; if there's a streaming outage we fall back to non-streaming responses (acceptable but UX-degrading).

Two asks:
1) Can you share the expected network egress IPs or a CIDR range for EU routing? Procurement will need this for the firewall rules.
2) Can Nikhil include estimated cost delta for dedicated EU capacity vs routing to US during low utilization?

I'll loop procurement once we have the IP/CIDR list.

Best,
Sam
Director of Product, Finova
sam.patel@finova.com

Hi Sam -

Thanks for the details. A few technical notes and attachments (network-topology.png included):

- Egress IPs / firewall: For EU-dedicated routing we can provide a stable CIDR block per deployment. I'll coordinate with infra to get the exact /24 range, but planning estimate attached.
- EU residency enforcement: We support region-tagging for requests and can enforce strict routing so EU-tagged requests never leave EU nodes. For disaster recovery we offer an opt-in asynchronous cross-region backup that stores only encrypted audit logs (no live KV).
- Cost delta: ballpark - dedicated EU capacity is ~25-35% premium vs shared global routing given current GPU pricing and reserved pools. Exact numbers depend on concurrency and sustained throughput; I'll add a small table in the SLA draft.
- Streaming and cancellations: our runtime supports token-level streaming with mid-stream cancels. For worst-case tail latency we recommend a small buffer (10-20ms) and a retry policy fallback to a slightly lower model variant to meet p95 constraints under burst.

Next steps from infra side:
- I'll send the CIDR and a short network checklist by EOD tomorrow.
- If procurement wants a dedicated quote, Aditya can jump in to provide committed capacity pricing.

-Nikhil
